newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD-Hong Kong stocks seen resilient.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD-Hong Kong stocks seen resilient.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to put on a brave face in the event of some likely profit-taking in the week ahead and the Hang Seng index should be able to break more records before the week is out, analysts said.

"I suspect we may see a little bit more profit-taking but I think it will be fairly shallow profit-taking," said Howard Gorges, director at South China Brokerage. "I would not be surprised by the end of the week if the market is back above 13,000," he said.
The Hang Seng index rose above the 13,000 point mark for the first time last week, reaching an intra-day record high at 13,054.91 on Friday before closing the day down 115.43 points at 12,889.37.
Despite Friday's loss, the blue-chip index rose 138.21 points, or 1.08 percent, last week.

"I think to a certain extent it is liquidity driven," said Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "Continued benign data from the United States will continue to help bond yields in the short term which should benefit Hong Kong. I think if the money is there, there is the potential to break new highs next week."

Analysts said although valuations in Hong Kong looked high compared with historical levels, economic growth in the territory and the corporate earnings outlook should underpin a continued rise in price earnings (PE) multiples.
"I think the market will be re-rated a bit higher next year on the settlement of the 1997 question and one way or another we will benefit from more inflow from China," said Gorges.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight next June 30.

Share prices are trading at about 14 times 1997 earnings, analysts said. Hutcheson said this compares with a range of about eight to 22 times over the past 10 years and an average of less than 12 times.

"During the next year it will go higher so one should not be too over-awed by the fact that we have had a good run in the market," said Gorges. "I think the PE is likely to go up to around 16 (next year)."
Gorges expects a range of between 12,700 and 13,100 points for the Hang Seng in the coming week.

He expects earnings growth of around 15 percent in the territory next year. Property companies are expected to benefit from continued strong demand for residential units, and a healthy Chinese economy should bolster Hong Kong earnings.

"Analysts have been upgrading (earnings) numbers over the last three months, whereas in many areas around the region they have been downgrading," said Hutcheson. "If I am looking around the region at what looks attractive, Hong Kong as a whole seems to look better than others."
Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities, said the market's rapid ascent had limited the upside potential in the short term but liquidity should continue to help prices.
"I think foreign funds are still looking for investment opportunities in the region so the market will continue to surge as long as there is liquidity," he said.
Kwong saw the Hang Seng moving between 12,800 and 13,100 points in the week ahead.
